title: Thrust Lever Assembly — Breakout Force Check
abstract: Breakout force check of both thrust levers, with the measurement method, the acceptance band and the lubrication that follows a check within limits.

sections.purpose: This task gives the breakout force check of both thrust levers, at the scheduled lubrication interval or following a crew report that the levers feel notchy or stiff.
sections.job_setup_note: Measure with the pedestal cold and the aircraft on external power only; a lever measured after a long flight reads low. Use the calibrated force gauge with the lever adapter and pull along the lever arc, not vertically. The acceptance band is sixteen to twenty-six newtons and the lubrication interval is twelve months.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm the pedestal is cold and the aircraft is on external power. 2. Fit the lever adapter to the first thrust lever. 3. Apply a slowly increasing force along the lever arc and record the force at which movement starts. 4. Repeat twice and take the mean of the three readings. 5. Repeat for the second lever. 6. Compare both means against the acceptance band of sixteen to twenty-six newtons. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT APPLY FORCE ACROSS THE LEVER ARC. A SIDE LOAD DAMAGES THE QUADRANT BEARING AND GIVES A HIGH READING. 8. If both readings are inside the band, apply the specified lubricant sparingly at the points shown in the figure and set the next check twelve months ahead. 9. WARNING: DO NOT USE A LUBRICANT OTHER THAN THE ONE SPECIFIED. THE DELIVERED SEAL COMPOUND SWELLS ON CONTACT WITH SOME SUBSTITUTES AND THE FORCE WILL RISE FURTHER. 10. If either reading is outside the band, do not lubricate; raise the seal and clamp replacement instead. 11. Check autothrust engagement and disconnect at both levers. 12. Record both means and the action taken.
sections.close_out: Close the pedestal access panel and confirm no tool remains inside. Confirm the flight deck is free of cautions. Record the breakout forces, the lubricant batch and the next due date in the aircraft technical log.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Twelve month lubrication interval.

safety_precautions: Do not use a lubricant other than the one specified.

tooling.description: Breakout force gauge 0-60 N with lever adapter

title: Thrust Lever Assembly — Breakout Force Check

issue.reason: Single interval and acceptance figure replaced by a table keyed to the friction seal standard, which is where the interval is now held.

abstract: Breakout force check of both thrust levers, with the measurement method, the acceptance band that depends on the friction seal standard fitted and the lubrication that follows a check within limits.

sections.purpose: This task gives the breakout force check of both thrust levers, at the scheduled lubrication interval or following a crew report that the levers feel notchy or stiff.
sections.job_setup_note: Measure with the pedestal cold and the aircraft on external power only; a lever measured after a long flight reads low. Use the calibrated force gauge with the lever adapter and pull along the lever arc, not vertically. Note the friction seal standard fitted before you compare against the acceptance band, because the delivered and the compatible seal standards have different bands and different lubrication intervals. The two are given together in the interval table in the figure: delivered seal, band sixteen to twenty-six newtons, interval twelve months; compatible seal of MOD-168238, band sixteen to twenty-two newtons, interval twenty-four months. The interval is held here and not in the modification dossier, so this table is the only place a planner can read it.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm the pedestal is cold and the aircraft is on external power. 2. Fit the lever adapter to the first thrust lever. 3. Apply a slowly increasing force along the lever arc and record the force at which movement starts. 4. Repeat twice and take the mean of the three readings. 5. Repeat for the second lever. 6. Read the friction seal standard from the aircraft configuration record and compare both means against the acceptance band for that standard in the interval table. Both levers must be at the same standard; where they are not, the aircraft is part embodied and the delivered figures apply to it. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT APPLY FORCE ACROSS THE LEVER ARC. A SIDE LOAD DAMAGES THE QUADRANT BEARING AND GIVES A HIGH READING. 8. If both readings are inside the band, apply the specified lubricant sparingly at the points shown in the figure and set the next check from the interval column of the same table row. 9. WARNING: DO NOT USE A LUBRICANT OTHER THAN THE ONE SPECIFIED. THE DELIVERED SEAL COMPOUND SWELLS ON CONTACT WITH SOME SUBSTITUTES AND THE FORCE WILL RISE FURTHER. 10. If either reading is outside the band, do not lubricate; raise the seal and clamp replacement instead. 11. Check autothrust engagement and disconnect at both levers. 12. Record both means, the table row used and the action taken.
sections.close_out: Close the pedestal access panel and confirm no tool remains inside. Confirm the flight deck is free of cautions. Record the breakout forces, the seal standard, the lubricant batch and the next due interval in the aircraft technical log.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The acceptance band and the lubrication interval are read from the interval table by friction seal standard: twelve months on the delivered seal, twenty-four months on the compatible seal of MOD-168238 with both levers converted. An aircraft with one lever converted stays on the twelve month row.

safety_precautions: Do not use a lubricant other than the one specified.

tooling.description: Breakout force gauge 0-60 N with lever adapter
